results.notes:
Side effects of this audit:
- I created and then removed three temp folders under SP (_audit_aa7_patchtest_tmp, _audit_g3_patchtest_tmp, _audit_g3_patchtest_tmp2). I also briefly wrote two listing files (.audit_live.txt and .audit_clone.txt) at the SP top level and removed them. The SP top level is back to its original 9 entries.
- My diff -rq of MAIN/retrux-web against aa3_base most likely made iCloud download 17 evicted files in MAIN/retrux-web: the dataless count went from 796 to 779. Their content is unchanged, and nothing was edited, moved or committed.
- I read no .env or credential file.

Risk worth telling the user:
- ~/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes is a symlink to the only copy of the 15 lanes. A cleaner that follows symlinks (or 'rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/*/' with a trailing slash) would delete the lanes through it. The safest step is to remove just the link before cleaning ('rm ~/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes'); resume step (1) already recreates it.
- The user should also be told not to delete ~/RetruxR11Work, or ~/Downloads/GI Discovery Deck until the pw165 copy above is made.
- MAIN still has 779 iCloud-evicted files: 775 in .next/dev, plus tsbuildinfo, .vercel/project.json, .vercel/README.txt and .env.local. They live in iCloud, so they are durable.
- The Vercel staging non-git copy was already lost in the earlier reboot. Its recipe is in the staging-deploy memory: re-link the project retrux-staging.
